turns.en: We basically don't think we're allowed to fail on this project. Oh, that's the thing. Great. We're just going to bet that the LLM flow is going to work and we'll make it work and we will hill climb all we need to burn the boats and just make this thing work.
turns.zh: 我们基本上觉得，在这个项目上我们不被允许失败。哦，原来症结在这儿。太好了。那我们就赌 LLM 这条路能走通，我们会让它走通，我们会一路爬坡优化，把需要的东西都搞到位——破釜沉舟，就是要把这事儿做成。

turns.en: And then they were like, Oh, okay, great. Do you want a next product review tomorrow, but is this like anything where you're like, I would not have guessed that was their blocker. And you saw that and they were like going.
turns.zh: 然后他们就说：哦，好，太好了。要不要明天再来一次产品评审？——那有没有那种，你会觉得“我真没想到卡住他们的居然是这个”、然后你亲眼看到他们就这样卡在那儿的情况？

turns.en: You mentioned the talent were thing before there's this big trend low margin high growth thing where from an investor's perspective, the funny example you gave of a lab or a tractor. Everyone wants something that can be that thing. Tell me about how you're going to be a hundred billion dollar business or a trillion dollar business.
turns.zh: 你之前提到人才争夺战这件事。现在有个大趋势——低利润率、高增长——从投资人的角度看，你举的那个“要么实验室、要么拖拉机”的好笑例子，人人都想要那种能成为“那个东西”的标的。跟我说说，你打算怎么把 Vanta 做成一家一千亿美元、甚至一万亿美元的公司？

turns.en: Somehow now every business needs to be that big. What's that like to face down where you need not see building a business that should be a hundred billion dollar business. There's like a hundred of those in the world. There's not that many. Yeah. And it's not to think Vanta won't be.
turns.zh: 现在莫名其妙地，每家公司都得有那么大。要去面对这种压力是什么感觉——你并不是在建一家本该值一千亿美元的公司。这样的公司全世界也就一百来家，没那么多。是的。而且我不是说 Vanta 成不了。

turns.en: It's funny for me. It's like, Oh, should I adjust the pitch and be like, well, inevitably the baseline here is Vanta's 50 billion. The real question you should be considering if you join, can you take us on a journey to like 250 billion.
turns.zh: 对我来说这事儿挺好笑的：哦，我要不要调整一下招募说辞，变成“呃，这里的基准前提是 Vanta 值 500 亿，你真正该考虑的问题是——如果你加入，你能不能带我们走上这段旅程、冲到 2,500 亿”？

turns.en: Should I just start saying that probably not, but the answer is not definitely not totally because you're like, well, that is the pitch that people who work at Vanta are getting from other companies. The market now is saying that so much. You do seem unambitious. So what do you do?
turns.zh: 我要不要就这么说？大概不该。但答案也绝不是“肯定不行”。因为现实是，这正是 Vanta 的员工从别的公司那里听到的说辞——如今市场就是这么讲的。你要是[不这么讲]，就显得你没野心。那你能怎么办？

turns.en: There's a Vanta principle value principle of do what it says on the tin. Do what you say you're going to do. I'm like, you can put ambitious and got a tin. It's not that don't over promise and under deliver. What we do is give some of that. Here's what we do as a company. Good, bad and different. Here's the context.
turns.zh: Vanta 有一条价值原则，叫“罐子上写什么就是什么”（do what it says on the tin）——说到做到。我会说：你可以把“有野心”写在罐子上，但别过度承诺、兑现不足。我们的做法是把一部分如实交代：这就是我们作为一家公司的样子，好的、坏的、不一样的都说，这是背景。

turns.en: Now, let me talk to you about the business metrics and we'll generally just show candidate to like show everybody everything. It's fine. They're good. We don't really want them to leak, but if they leak, it's not the worst. Walk them through that and what we're doing and how that grows over time.
turns.zh: 接下来我再跟你聊聊业务指标。我们基本上会把所有东西都给候选人看，几乎是对所有人敞开。这没关系，数据挺好的。我们其实不太希望它外泄，但就算泄了也不算最糟。我们会带他们过一遍我们在做什么、这些数字随时间怎么增长，

turns.en: Try to root it in all of the facts and all of the data. And so in some ways it's counter the vibes with data and trustworthy vibes versus yellow vibes. What is it like in those talent wars? If the most talented people are being told this thing's going to go to a trillion.
turns.zh: 尽量把一切都落在事实和数据上。所以某种意义上，这是用数据去对抗“氛围”（vibes）——用可信的氛围，去对抗那种虚浮的氛围。——在那种人才争夺战里，如果最有才华的人被告知“这家公司会冲到一万亿”，那是什么感觉？

turns.en: Basically, every other company that's trying to hire them. Well, the better one is well, we're six billion today. But Sequoia is going to do a $10 billion check in a month. And then somebody's going to write it up to 25 next year. But we can get you in at six today. That's a good one. That would stuff.
turns.zh: 基本上，其他每一家想招他们的公司都这么讲。呃，还有一个更“高明”的版本：“呃，我们今天值 60 亿，但红杉（Sequoia）一个月后会开一张 100 亿的支票，然后明年就会有人把估值写到 250 亿。不过我们今天能让你按 60 亿进场。”这个说辞很厉害，能把人忽悠住。

turns.en: So your face at that. Like, what do you do? Do you not want those people? Maybe it's a filter. Sometimes I think if you go to the person and be like, what are you optimizing for? Why did you entertain that? But not in a pokey way. Just what's annoying you, Advanta? One of these in specific. Very strong leader. Still a phanta.
turns.zh: 所以你面对这种局面，怎么办？你是不是不想要那些人？也许这反倒是一种筛选。有时候我会想，如果你去问那个人：你在优化什么？你为什么会考虑它？——但不是带着指责的意思，只是问：Vanta 到底哪里让你不爽？这里面有一个具体的例子：一位非常强的领导者，至今还在 Vanta。

turns.en: It was basically this person felt like they couldn't make decisions that would put Vanta on a similar trajectory. And that would be their preference. But they're like, oh, but this new place is promising me full decision making authority on this trajectory.
turns.zh: 基本上就是，这个人觉得自己在 Vanta 没法做出那种能把公司推上相似轨迹的决策，而那本来是更合他心意的选择。他就会想：哦，可这家新公司承诺给我在这条轨迹上的完全决策权。

turns.en: Totally fair feedback. What do you need to feel like you make these decisions? Like just go make these decisions. Go. There's a money part and a formal part for sure. We've definitely gone up on comp and comp is kind of a joke. Now the compound is whatever data you have is wrong.
turns.zh: 这是完全合理的反馈。你需要什么才能觉得自己能做这些决策？那就直接去做这些决策啊，去做。这里面确实有钱的部分、也有正式授权的部分。我们绝对提高了薪酬——而“薪酬”现在几乎成了个笑话，因为你手里无论有什么数据，都是错的。

turns.en: It is what is being offered to these people. How much more do you pay the top person advantage than you did? Like as a multiple versus like. Oh, I think we should have way more compass version than we do. So that's interesting. But if I go five years back and that person made X dollars, what multiple of X does the person make now?
turns.zh: 它就是这些人正在被开出的价码。你现在给 Vanta 顶尖人才开的价，比你过去高多少？比如按倍数算。——哦，我觉得我们应该给远高于现在水平的薪酬，所以这很有意思。但如果我回到五年前，那个人当时拿 X 美元，现在这个人拿的是 X 的多少倍？

turns.en: It's probably like a factor of 10. Wow. I think it actually should be higher. My comp philosophy is you never pay the top people enough enough. You should always try and you will never hit it. And there's a bunch of people you pay much more than their contribution.
turns.zh: 大概是 10 倍。哇。我觉得其实还应该更高。我的薪酬哲学是：对最顶尖的人，你永远给不够、永远给不到位。你应该一直努力去给，但你永远达不到那个点。而且有一批人，你付给他们的钱远超其实际贡献。

turns.en: Say a bit more about what those top people are doing that's so valuable typically. High agency get shit done. That sounds so milk toast and that's worth millions of dollars. But yes, actually it is a high context person who understands the company and the customers and the domain.
turns.zh: 再多说说，这些顶尖的人到底在做什么，这么有价值？——通常就是高能动性（high agency）、能把事办成。这听着平淡无奇，却值好几百万美元。但没错，它确实值钱：这是一个高上下文的人，懂公司、懂客户、懂这个领域，

turns.en: Making generally reasonable decisions and sometimes bad ones and then iterating on their bad ones and just moving is so valuable. That would be 10 X again in five more years. Or is that starting to get too crazy? Is the rate at which the most valuable people are getting more valuable staying the same accelerating.
turns.zh: 能做出大体合理的决策、偶尔也做错的，然后在自己做错的地方迭代，就是不停地往前推进——这太有价值了。——那再过五年，这又会翻 10 倍吗？还是说那开始太离谱了？最有价值的人变得越来越有价值，这个速率是保持不变，还是在加速？

turns.en: Accelerating the counter force is at what point will investors get more concerned about dilution and stock based comp, which they weren't throughout the 2010s late 2010s. We had more of a like stock based conversation as an industry in like 2022, 23 now we're definitely not talking about it.
turns.zh: 在加速。反作用力在于：投资人到哪个节点会开始更在意股权稀释和基于股票的薪酬？在整个 2010 年代、2010 年代后期，他们并不太在意。我们作为一个行业，在 2022、2023 年更多有过一场关于股权激励的讨论，而现在我们绝对不再谈它了。

turns.en: That's the counter sign without that push on like dilution. I think people just get paid more and more. That's probably probably shut. How much you care about your valuation and multiple and the engineering of those things.
turns.zh: 这就是那股反向的推力——没有了在稀释问题上的这种施压，我觉得人们就是会被付得越来越多。这大概是对的。——你有多在意自己的估值和倍数，以及对这些东西的“工程化运作”？

turns.en: I've historically not cared and sometimes even done things to like demonstrate by not caring. I care about error and error growth. I pay a ton of attention to those and those in the metrics. I think I've now been through enough valuation environments like 20 times 2021, 2022 seen the like multiple roller coaster.
turns.zh: 我一向不太在意，有时甚至会故意做些事来表明我不在意。我在意的是 ARR（年度经常性收入）和 ARR 增长，我对这两个指标投入大量关注，它们才是我真正看重的数字。我想我现在已经经历过足够多的估值环境了——2021、2022 那种，见过倍数像过山车一样起伏。

turns.en: I just don't put a bunch of stock in that I used to not. I think the thing I care a bunch about that then get me to caring about these multiples is the sentiment of people who work at Vanta.
turns.zh: 我就是不会在那上面押太多注，我以前会。我觉得我真正很在意、进而让我开始在意这些倍数的东西，是 Vanta 员工的情绪。

turns.en: And did they feel like they're at a company that is growing and growing and growing and then in general growing and then growing relative to other their other opportunities in the market. There's a part of the market that is raising money every six months that 5x supplier valuation and that's a real talent competitor.
turns.zh: 他们会不会觉得自己身处一家在增长、增长、再增长的公司，而且是相对于他们在市场上的其他机会而言也在增长。市场里有一部分公司每六个月就融一次资，估值翻五倍，那是实实在在的人才竞争对手。

turns.en: And what about things like tenders? Have you done this historically? We have not done them historically, but the game on the field is you're doing a tender every time and you got to do them. Does this feel unhealthy? My opinion about it don't matter and have all the feelings I want in whatever direction about tenders.
turns.zh: ——那像 tender（老股要约回购）这类东西呢？你们以前做过吗？我们以前没做过，但摆在明面上的现实是：你现在每次融资都在做 tender，而且你必须做。这事儿会不会显得不太健康？我对它的看法并不重要，我可以对 tender 有各种各样的感受，往哪个方向都行。

turns.en: They are normalized and people expect them and they expected as part of their comp. And if you are not given it to them, you got to give them a bunch of other stuff to make it up. How does all this affect your exit ambitions to go public or to be sold or realize some end game for Vanta not at all?
turns.zh: 但它们已经被常态化了，人们期待它、把它当成自己薪酬的一部分。如果你不给，你就得给一堆别的东西来补偿。——那这一切会怎么影响你的退出雄心：去上市、被收购，或者为 Vanta 实现某种终局？完全不影响？

turns.en: Not really, which is the again, a very founder privilege statement, but the end game is how long can we keep this going for and 99% of the big independent software companies in the United States are public. Yes, IPO in that sense. I don't have it as a bucket list item myself.
turns.zh: 真不太影响，而这又是一个非常“创始人才有资格说”的话。但终局在于：我们能把这件事持续做多久。美国 99% 的大型独立软件公司都是上市的。是的，从这个意义上说就是 IPO。不过对我个人来说，它并不是一个人生愿望清单项目。

turns.en: It's more of like means to an end lots of people during companies and want the bucket list item. So founder privilege caveat here again, but goal is big independent standalone company. And all this stuff tools for building ways of building kind of these kinds of things I'm asking about. What do you think is over hyped and under hyped?
turns.zh: 它更像是一种达成目的的手段。很多人创办公司，就是想要那个愿望清单项目。所以这里又有个“创始人特权”的前提，但目标就是一家大型的、独立的、自主经营的公司。——而在所有这些“构建的工具、构建的方式”里，也就是我在问的这些，你觉得什么被高估了、什么被低估了？

turns.en: Under hyped is knowing the company and the customers relative to knowing the skill set. It is still really hard to hire train on board make effective people who join a company. Company meetings make this better and easier and like put information and fingertips.
turns.zh: 被低估的，是“懂公司、懂客户”相对于“懂某项技能”的价值。要把一个人招进来、培训、引导、让他真正发挥作用，到现在依然非常难。公司的各种会议确实让这件事更好、更容易，能把信息放到你指尖。

turns.en: But there is still totally something to be said about someone who's been in a company knows how to navigate the company knows customers all of that. I met a few is right now where we value that skill set more than like the vertical skill set of your good at sales your good at customer success.
turns.zh: 但有一点仍然绝对成立：一个在公司待过的人，知道怎么在公司里游刃有余、了解客户，等等。我现在处于这样一种状态——我们把这种技能看得比垂直技能更重，也就是比“你擅长销售、你擅长客户成功”更重，

turns.en: And would take a worse sales person on sale skill who knows the Vanta pieces more. There's something in that and I think especially as a lot of the web that's going to be building out go to marketing. I think they're actually very much evaluating your good sales person. That's slightly off.
turns.zh: 我们宁愿要一个销售技能稍差、但更懂 Vanta 这套东西的人，也不要一个纯销售能力强的人。这里面有点道理。我觉得尤其是很多将要去做市场拓展（go-to-market）的人，他们其实非常看重“你是不是很棒的销售”——这判断有点偏。

turns.en: And then I think as we think about building agents for all of this, the company context piece. The customer context piece is probably being relatively undervalued to like you are good sales person. That the less valuable skill slightly today than it was four years ago.
turns.zh: 然后我觉得，当我们想到为这一切构建智能体时，“懂公司”这块上下文、“懂客户”这块上下文，很可能被相对低估了；而“你是个很棒的销售”这项技能，如今的价值比四年前略微低了一些。

turns.en: What about over hyped token for racing low margins for the sake of having low margins. Custom training models for the marketing value. We all to say we post train to model on our stuff explain why go top to the inference providers and sometimes give them depending on the provider give them true serum.
turns.zh: ——那被高估的呢？刷 token（token farming）、为了低利润率而低利润率、为了营销价值去定制训练模型。我们都想说“我们在自己的数据上后训练（post-train）了一个模型”。去问问那些推理服务商（inference providers）吧，解释一下为什么要这么做——有时候你还要视服务商而定，把真实数据交给他们。

turns.en: They will say like look, the reason to post train a model is cost some businesses have that need. But there is not a quality reason to do it. There's kind of a marketing reason to do it right now in this environment.
turns.zh: 他们会说：看，后训练一个模型的理由是成本，有些业务确实有这个需求。但从质量角度并没有理由这么做。在当前这种环境下，做它更多是出于一种营销上的理由。

turns.en: And I think there's a lot of post training for marketing reasons for investors and for customers, mostly for investors actually. If one of those people were pitching the other side of this, the value of post training. What is the pitch to you when this company comes to you and it's like we'll do XYZ for you.
turns.zh: 而且我觉得现在有很多后训练是出于营销目的——面向投资人，也面向客户，但其实主要是面向投资人。如果让其中一方来推销这件事的另一面，也就是后训练的价值，那么当这样一家公司来找你、说“我们会替你做 XYZ”时，他们对你说的是什么？他们声称好处在哪里？

turns.en: What are they saying and where they say the benefits are you are putting a stake in the ground of being a really eye company. Customers will notice. I think that's the primary one. I do think there's a secondary one in some use cases of like a form factor thing.
turns.zh: 你是在立一个 flag，表明自己是一家真正的 AI 公司，客户会注意到——我觉得这是首要的那条理由。我确实认为在某些用例里还有第二条理由，跟形态（form factor）有关。

turns.en: And I think especially with large enterprises, you want to deploy this piece of software wall to wall that requires integrations and 17 people to sign off. That's a whole thing. Why don't you just give them a like model specific to them for this use case. I don't know. So if I was one of these people and I came into Vanta.
turns.zh: 尤其是面对大型企业时，你想把这块软件在整个公司范围内铺开部署，这需要集成、需要 17 个人签字批准，那是一整套麻烦事。那你为什么不干脆给他们一个专门用于这个用例、专属于他们的模型呢？我也说不好。——所以如果我是这些人当中的一个，来到 Vanta，

turns.en: What does post training literally mean? What would it mean in your context? What are you doing? What are the steps that you would go through? So we would need a bunch of data from that specific customer and then go right a bunch of evil then change model weights based on that customer specific data.
turns.zh: “后训练”到底字面上是什么意思？在你的语境里它会意味着什么？你们会做什么？会经过哪些步骤？——我们需要从那个特定客户那里拿到一大堆数据，然后写一大堆 eval（评估），再基于这些客户专属的数据去改动模型权重。

turns.en: The process would be they're trying to achieve something. They've got some data. You tune a model to achieve the thing. Increase the evil and then sell them that. Exactly. On an ongoing basis. And your point is that that's overrated because it doesn't actually improve their. It can. I think I'm a skeptical.
turns.zh: 这个流程就是：他们想达成某个目标，他们手上有一些数据，你去调一个模型来达成那个目标、把 eval 分数提上去，然后再把它卖给他们。没错。而且是持续地卖。你的意思是这东西被高估了，因为它其实并不能真正改善他们的效果。它可以改善，但我持怀疑态度。

turns.en: I was like, does everyone really want to be handed a model or they're so much around that from user experience perspective from a deployment perspective form factor. It feels a little like. You know the social media with like your mobile apps when we like we hadn't figured out pulled a refresh yet.
turns.zh: 我会想：大家真的愿意被塞一个模型吗？围绕它有那么多东西——从用户体验、从部署、从形态的角度看。它有点像……你知道，早期社交媒体配移动端 App 的时候，我们还没搞出“下拉刷新”（pull to refresh）那阵子。

turns.en: I don't think anyone actually wants to be handed a model. The same way it's like hitting a refresh button. I don't know that's on silly, but that's what we did in 2011. There's some version of that here. We haven't figured out how this actually works and handing models.
turns.zh: 我不觉得有谁真的想被塞一个模型，就像没人真的想按一个刷新按钮一样。我不知道，那听起来很蠢，但 2011 年我们就是这么干的。所以这里也有某个类似的阶段：我们还没搞清楚这东西到底该怎么运作，而“把模型塞给用户”——
